text_nodes.text: Texas put AI in a money class.
The board's own course text tells a student to research career pathways using artificial intelligence tools.
Texas State Board of Education 19 TAC section 113.26

text_nodes.text: The verb is research. The student does it, and the course text names the tool.
19 TAC Chapter 113, Subchapter C §113.26. Personal Financial Literacy and Economics
(d)(3) Careers, postsecondary education, and earning potential. The student is expected to:

(C) research career pathways using labor-market data, online resources, and artificial intelligence tools to evaluate income growth, employment trends, global competition, comparative advantage, technological change, creative destruction, required skills, and possible employers
Knowledge statement (3) Careers and earning potential
c14 c18 c19 TEXAS AI DOCKET
The statute the board cites makes it responsible for graduation requirements, and treats the half credit as one a student must comply with.
Taught from the school year that opens in 2027.
One half credit on completion, and a curriculum requirement rather than an elective by the statute the board cites.

Ten chapters. The machine is in three.
Every chapter of the course text is a thing a student must be able to do with money. Seven of them carry none of the four machine terms.
